subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, and parent/channel notification behavior should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds config/default behavior, mutating child-run recovery, session queue unblocking, and user-visible channel semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the policy from source evidence alone.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default/opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity and kill/reap work.

options.title: Prototype default-off watchdog
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in implementation first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until maintainers accept defaults.

options.title: Defer automatic recovery
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill yet; rely on explicit `runTimeoutSeconds`, diagnostics recovery, and future manual kill/reap controls until more production evidence or policy direction exists.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default/opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity and kill/reap work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest current-main history across the subagent registry/control boundary and adjacent timeout semantics that this policy would extend.
